attributes.probed_form: AXIS 1 (REVERTED). Hypothesis: `u32 tmp` is address-taken at `qv = *(f32*)&tmp;`, which pins the whole variable to a stack home and forces a store at each of its five assignments; giving the reinterpret its own variable should leave the other four uses register-resident. Added declaration `u32 qbits;` immediately after `u32 tmp;`, and replaced exactly `tmp = pbSwap32(data[idx - 2]); qv = *(f32*)&tmp;` with `qbits = pbSwap32(data[idx - 2]); qv = *(f32*)&qbits;`. AXIS 2 (REVERTED). Hypothesis: pbSwap32's two distinct unions `a, b` let MWCC prove no-alias and pipeline the four loads ahead of the stores, where target strictly alternates lbz/stb through a single register; a single in-place union forces the dependency. Replaced the body of `static u32 pbSwap32(u32 x)` with exactly: `union { u32 w; u8 b[4]; } a; u8 t; a.w = x; t = a.b[0]; a.b[0] = a.b[3]; a.b[3] = t; t = a.b[1]; a.b[1] = a.b[2]; a.b[2] = t; return a.w;`.
attributes.residual:
NO SOURCE CHANGE RETAINED; the TU is byte-identical to its pre-pass state. Baseline reproduced the prior record exactly and is therefore live: fuzzy 86.9230%, real 1162, insns T1013/O1017, multiset 36t, frame T904/O904.

REFUTATION 1, THE PRIOR RECORD'S DOMINANT-CLUSTER MECHANISM IS WRONG. The prior record named the ~50-instruction cluster at target @0x65c-0x750 an 'arm-order/basic-block-layout difference' in the two three-armed format chains and made the arm-swap law the next agent's first move. The aligned read settles it: the cfmt chain carries the SAME arm order and the SAME branch structure on both sides -- target `cmpwi 109; bne; <0x6D arm>; b; cmpwi 102; bne; <0x66 arm>; b; <else arm>` against ours `cmpwi 109; bne; <0x6D arm>; b; cmpwi 102; bne; <0x66 arm>; b; <else arm>` -- and the neighbouring two-armed `clrlwi/cmplwi 3` test (source line 893, not a format chain at all) likewise matches arm for arm. There is no arm to swap. The arm-swap axis on this function is CLOSED without a probe being spent on it.

WHAT THE CLUSTER ACTUALLY IS, from the same read, two separable things. (a) cnt RESIDENCY: target holds cnt in a callee-saved register (r25) across the whole chain, while ours reloads it with `lwz r4,324(r1)` in exactly the two arms that use it (the 0x6D and else arms); the 0x66 arm, which uses step rather than cnt, reloads nothing. (b) tmp STORE TRAFFIC: ours emits a `stw ...,364(r1)` after each pbSwap32 result that target does not.

REFUTATION 2, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART. Both probes attacked (b) and both went the WRONG WAY, which inverts the reading of the evidence. Splitting the address-taken `tmp` moved real 1162 -> 1328 and the multiset 36t -> 46t, and flipped the store population's sign: the baseline had ours carrying 3 surplus stw, and after the split TARGET carried 3 surplus stw plus 6 stb and 7 lbz. So target genuinely HAS that store traffic, the single shared address-taken `tmp` is the CORRECT source shape, and its stack home is not a defect to be removed. The in-place single-union pbSwap32 moved real 1162 -> 1257 and 36t -> 39t, so the existing two-union form is also correct. Two independent probes therefore CONFIRM the current source shape rather than improving it.

NEXT AGENT: do NOT retry the arm swap (precondition measured false), the tmp-web split (measured, real 1328), or the in-place union swap (measured, real 1257). The live residual is the prior record's mechanism (2) -- indexed addressing, target `lwzx` against our `add`+`lwz`, confirmed present at @0x474 in this pass's diff -- plus mechanism (3), the byte round-trip at @0xbd8/@0xc1c/@0xc60, plus the newly named cnt-residency reload in the cfmt chain. Note that (2) is guarded by the address-PRE law and is not a respelling job, and that any frame-growing form is constrained by the frame already being EQUAL.
